1915-B03050087600.summary: Sun Yat-sen in Tokyo to Soong Ching-ling ('Laisaosang' / 'Rosamonde') in Shanghai, Japanese Communications Bureau copies: love telegrams, Yung the rival suitor, 'Reply by cipher ... they can get our secrets by guessing'. Readings are Brice Dudout's (contributed); only the 20 and 26 Feb forms were transcribed and re-deciphered here, his transcriptions of the others are not published.

1915-B03050087700.summary: Sun to Ching-ling about her return by the steamer Korea (12 and 15 Mar), 'Are you forgot me?' (10 Jun), and Ching-ling's 'Lovesick ... in torture. Be merciful. Come or free me forever' (7 Jul). Brice Dudout's readings; only the 7 Jul form was transcribed and re-deciphered here.

1916-B03050089000.summary: Between Shanghai and 'Rosamonde Tokio' after Sun's return to China, May 1916: his safe landing in the French concession, Canton, and repeated orders to leave the iron trunk in Mr Inuzuka's care. Brice Dudout's readings; no cipher transcription of these forms is in the repository.

snip.cap: Tokyo to “Laisaosang, Shanghai”, 26 February 1915, signed 頭山滿: twelve cipher words, myovonoiho coohavbhea = “whenever ye see Yung you”
snip.credit: Diplomatic Archives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, JACAR B03050087600 image 52, via Brice Dudout’s wenmi repository

system: English telegraphic text, unspaced and cut into ten-letter words, enciphered by a reciprocal letter substitution (twelve swapped pairs, d and p unchanged).
